text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 13px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: C373 · Empirical models: fit the data, not the noise

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Book Sec. 9.3.1 (p. 316) · an empirical (equivalent-circuit) compact model = a suitable function fitted to measured or simulated data

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 1 · How an empirical compact model is built

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9.6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #f6f6f6
font-size: 8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Electronics does this already: a SPICE transistor model can have over 100 parameters, fitted to experimental (or simulated) data.

text.style: font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Tools: build an equivalent electrical circuit from measurements (e.g. ADS), or curve-fit a frequency response to polynomial or rational functions (e.g. MATLAB RF Toolbox).

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 2 · Right function: compact, and smooths the noise

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6
font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.6px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #30d158
font-size: 8.3px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: noise σ 0.30 dB, but the fit is only 0.02 dB (rms) from the truth

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 3 · Too many parameters: the fit copies the noise

text.style: font-size: 8.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: a linear resistor V = I·R: 12 synthetic points with noise (σ 40 mV)

text.style: font-size: 8.3px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: at the points: 1-param 44 mV, polynomial 12 mV (rms)

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.3px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #ff6961

g.text: vs truth: 1-param 15 mV, polynomial 50 mV → possibly an incorrect model

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 11px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: 4 · The main challenge — and the rule of thumb

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #f6f6f6
font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6
font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #f6f6f6
font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6
font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #f6f6f6
font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6
font-weight: 700; font-size: 8.9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #f6f6f6
font-size: 8.1px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6
font-weight: 700; font-size: 9.2px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Takeaway: fit data with the simplest suitable function — compact and smooth; too many parameters capture measurement errors.

text.style: font-size: 8px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: middle; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Next, Sec. 9.4: a polynomial (Eq. 9.2) and a rational function (Eq. 9.4) as compact models. Plots 2–3: synthetic data made for this figure — illustrative.
